section: Supreme Court - composition, appointment, collegium and NJAC, jurisdictions (original, appellate, advisory, writ)
subsections: Number of judges - who can increase it, present strength, Acts
Retired and ad hoc judges - Articles 127, 128; additional judges

accepted.s: The Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Act, 1956 was enacted under which constitutional provision relating to the composition of the Supreme Court?
accepted.x: Article 124(1) provides the constitutional basis for determining the number of judges of the Supreme Court. Parliament may increase the number by law, and such an amendment requires only a simple majority.
accepted.tq: Match the statutory mechanism with the correct constitutional provision.
accepted.sec: Number of judges - who can increase it, present strength, Acts  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the sanctioned strength of the Supreme Court, including the Chief Justice of India, in the years indicated?
accepted.x: The strength was 8 in 1950, 18 in 1977, 26 in 1986 and 31 from 2009. These figures include the Chief Justice of India.
accepted.tq: Use the complete numerical sequence rather than relying on a single familiar figure.
accepted.sec: Number of judges - who can increase it, present strength, Acts  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the strength of the Supreme Court:
1. The 2019 amendment raised the sanctioned strength to 34, including the Chief Justice of India.
2. The 2019 amendment received presidential assent on 10 August 2019.
3. The 2019 amendment replaced the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Act, 1956.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The 2019 amendment amended the 1956 Act; it did not replace it.
accepted.tq: Identify the wrong legislative relationship in the final statement.
accepted.sec: Number of judges - who can increase it, present strength, Acts  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to the 2026 increase in the strength of the Supreme Court, consider the following statements:
1. The Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Ordinance, 2026 was issued under Article 123.
2. The Ordinance was notified on 16 May 2026.
3. It replaced the figure 'thirty-three' with 'thirty-seven'.
4. A Bill to replace the Ordinance was listed for the Monsoon Session of 2026.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. The 2026 Ordinance was promulgated under Article 123, notified on 16 May, raised the number from 33 to 37 additional judges apart from the CJI, and was proposed to be replaced by a Bill in the Monsoon Session.
accepted.tq: Check each date, constitutional authority and legislative consequence separately.
accepted.sec: Number of judges - who can increase it, present strength, Acts  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following stages relating to the sanctioned strength of the Supreme Court in chronological order:
A. Strength fixed at 26
B. Strength fixed at 8
C. Strength fixed at 31
D. Strength fixed at 18
accepted.tq: Anchor the sequence with the earliest and latest strength figures.
accepted.sec: Number of judges - who can increase it, present strength, Acts  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under Article 127 of the Constitution, an ad hoc judge of the Supreme Court may be appointed when
o: the sanctioned strength of the Court is increased
a quorum of permanent judges is lacking
the office of the Chief Justice of India is vacant
a retired judge refuses to sit in the Court
accepted.x: Article 127 applies when there is no quorum of permanent judges available to hold or continue a sitting of the Supreme Court.
accepted.tq: Associate the exceptional appointment with the specific constitutional trigger.
accepted.sec: Retired and ad hoc judges - Articles 127, 128; additional judges  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about a retired judge sitting in the Supreme Court under Article 128:
1. The Chief Justice of India requires the President's previous consent.
2. The consent of the retired judge is required.
3. Such a judge exercises all the powers of a judge of the Supreme Court.
4. Such a judge is deemed to be a regular judge of the Supreme Court for all purposes.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. A retired judge sitting under Article 128 has the powers of a Supreme Court judge but is not deemed to be a regular judge of the Court.
accepted.tq: Spot the absolute legal status claim in the last statement.
accepted.sec: Retired and ad hoc judges - Articles 127, 128; additional judges  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding additional judges is correct?
o: Additional judges are appointed under Article 128 for temporary vacancies in the Supreme Court.
Additional judges exist in High Courts under Article 224, but there are no additional judges in the Supreme Court.
Additional judges may be appointed in the Supreme Court under Article 224.
Additional judges are appointed only in the Supreme Court when its workload increases.
accepted.x: Article 224 deals with additional and acting judges of High Courts. The Supreme Court has no provision for additional judges of this kind.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the similar-sounding categories attached to the Supreme Court and High Courts.
accepted.sec: Retired and ad hoc judges - Articles 127, 128; additional judges  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Article 131 confers exclusive original jurisdiction on the Supreme Court in which of the following disputes?
1. Between the Government of India and one or more States
2. Between the Government of India and some States on one side and other States on the other
3. Between two or more States
4. Between two private companies incorporated in different States
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 describe the federal disputes covered by Article 131. A dispute between private companies does not fall within this exclusive original jurisdiction.
accepted.tq: Separate federal-unit disputes from ordinary private litigation.

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT excluded from the exclusive original jurisdiction of the Supreme Court under Article 131?
o: An inter-State river-water dispute governed by Article 262
A dispute between the Government of India and one or more States concerning their legal rights
A dispute under a pre-Constitution treaty or agreement
A matter concerning the Finance Commission under Article 280
accepted.x: A dispute between the Union and one or more States concerning legal rights is within Article 131. Pre-Constitution agreements, inter-State river-water disputes and Finance Commission matters are excluded.
accepted.tq: Find the one included category among constitutionally excluded matters.

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Original jurisdiction over federal disputes — Article 131
Review of Supreme Court judgments — Article 143
accepted.x: Article 131 deals with the Supreme Court's original jurisdiction over federal disputes. Article 143 concerns advisory jurisdiction, Article 137 review, and Article 136 Special Leave to Appeal.
accepted.tq: Use the article-number distinction among closely related Supreme Court jurisdictions.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Supreme Court's jurisdiction under Article 32 is original in nature.
2. Article 32 jurisdiction is exclusive to the Supreme Court because High Courts cannot issue writs for enforcement of Fundamental Rights.
3. The Supreme Court's original jurisdiction under Article 131 is exclusive in respect of the specified federal disputes.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Article 32 gives the Supreme Court original writ jurisdiction, but it is not exclusive because High Courts may issue writs under Article 226.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between original jurisdiction that is exclusive and original jurisdiction shared with High Courts.

accepted.s: The jurisdiction to decide disputes relating to the election of the President and Vice-President of India is
o: appellate jurisdiction of the Supreme Court under Article 136
original jurisdiction of the High Courts under Article 226
original, exclusive and final jurisdiction of the Supreme Court under Article 71
advisory jurisdiction of the Supreme Court under Article 143
accepted.x: Article 71 vests the Supreme Court with original, exclusive and final jurisdiction over disputes concerning the election of the President and Vice-President.
accepted.tq: Link the special election jurisdiction with its distinctive constitutional features.

accepted.s:
Which of the following matters falls outside the original jurisdiction of the Supreme Court?
1. An election dispute concerning the Parliament
2. An election dispute concerning a State Legislature
3. A dispute between two or more States
4. A dispute between the Union and one or more States
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Election disputes concerning Parliament and State Legislatures are outside the Supreme Court's original jurisdiction and ordinarily go to the High Courts. Union-State and inter-State federal disputes are covered by Article 131.
accepted.tq: Separate legislative election disputes from Article 131 federal disputes.

accepted.s: The curative petition jurisdiction of the Supreme Court is associated with which of the following cases?
o: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala
Rupa Ashok Hurra v. Ashok Hurra
I. R. Coelho v. State of Tamil Nadu
S. R. Bommai v. Union of India
accepted.x: The Supreme Court evolved the curative petition in Rupa Ashok Hurra v. Ashok Hurra (2002), permitting a limited remedy after dismissal of a review petition in exceptional circumstances.
accepted.tq: Associate the procedural innovation with the case that created it.
